blocks.content: The Circum-Pacific Belt, popularly known as the Pacific Ring of Fire, accounts for more than three-fourths of the world's active volcanoes.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Circum-Pacific Belt, popularly known as the Pacific 'Ring of Fire', contains over three-fourths of the world's active and dormant volcanoes.
The Mid-Atlantic Belt is characterized by constructive plate boundaries where basaltic fissure eruptions continuously generate new ocean floor.
The Mid-Continental Belt (Alpine-Himalayan Belt) experiences convergent continental collisions, housing Mediterranean volcanoes like Mt. Vesuvius, Mt. Etna, and Stromboli.
Intraplate volcanism occurs away from plate margins over isolated thermal mantle plumes, forming hotspot island chains like Hawaii and Reunion.

rows: Pacific Ring of Fire (Mt. Fuji, Mt. Cotopaxi)

items: Stromboli is frequently asked in exams as the 'Lighthouse of the Mediterranean' due to its continuous night-time visibility.
Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's sole active volcano, while Narcondam is classified as extinct/dormant.
Divergent boundaries produce quiet, fluid basaltic lava, whereas convergent boundaries form highly explosive, viscous andesitic lava.
